newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Trans-Asia joins Indonesian drilling group.
newsitem.headline: Trans-Asia joins Indonesian drilling group.

text.p: Trans-Asia Oil and Energy Development Corp said on Wednesday it had bought a three percent stake in a drilling consortium which will explore an offshore oil field in East Kalimantan in Indonesia.
"The Gosungan-I well is expected to be spudded later this month ... The well will be drilled at a water depth of 920 feet," Trans-Asia said in a statement.
The well will test the petroleum potential of the large carbonate build-up prospects in the area.
"Oil shows in the carbonate build-up penetrated by the Karang Besar-1 well, drilled 10 km west of Gosungan, demonstrate generation and migration of petroleum in this sub-basin," the company added.
The operator of the field is Maersk Oil Indonesia Karang Besar AS which owns 47.5 percent of the consortium. Another major investor is Canadian Petroleum Karang Besar Ltd.
Maersk Oil Indonesia is a unit of shipping and energy group Maersk, a subsidiary of A.P. Moeller group. Canadian Petroleum is a unit of Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd.
